obligation: G131 -- three resident Qwen3.8 workers stable, with MEASURED RSS and memory pressure
the_binding_resource_is_WIRED_not_RSS: each worker wires 15.59 GB and the model wired(n) = 4.63 + 15.59n reproduces its own measurement exactly at n=3 (51.41 predicted vs 51.41 measured, the value held by 29 of 43 samples). Wired memory is NOT reclaimable -- it cannot be compressed and cannot be swapped -- so it is a HARD ceiling and not a slow degradation. RSS is the number that looks alarming (49.4 GB of 103.1) and it is the wrong number to watch.
why_five_workers_CRASHED: at n=5 the projection wires 82.6 GB of 103.1 GB, leaving 20.5 GB for the OS, Metal kernel compilation, pack generation and all page cache. At n=3 the free page count already read 0.13-0.58 GB and the INACTIVE pool absorbed the demand, falling 44.0 -> 26.8 GB. At n=5 that buffer is gone. The directive's 'three, NOT five unless measured memory headroom proves safe' is now measured, and the mechanism has a name: unreclaimable wired growth of 15.59 GB per resident worker.

safe_ceiling.note: 4 is projected, not measured. 3 is measured.

concurrency_is_MEMORY_SAFE_and_THROUGHPU: three workers cost 2.51x per-worker latency (30.3 -> 76.2 ms/token) and buy only 1.19x aggregate throughput (33.0 -> 39.4 TPS). ONE worker already saturates the GPU; the other two mostly queue. This is the directive's protected GPU lane measured rather than assumed -- and it prices the rule precisely: parallel Qwen workers are nearly worthless for GPU work and free for CPU work, which is exactly the split 'serialize timing, parallelize cognition' prescribes.
any_timing_taken_under_concurrency_is_vo: a token time measured with three workers up reads 76.2 ms against a true 30.3 ms. A candidate benchmarked under load would look 2.5x worse than it is, and two candidates benchmarked under DIFFERENT load would rank arbitrarily. No timing in this campaign may be taken with a second worker resident.
